\clearpage

### Supplementary Note A: Software Implementation {.unnumbered}

DStressR is implemented as an R package for reproducible analysis of arrayed
promoter-reporter screens. The exported workflow follows the statistical
layers described in the main text. `prepare_assay()` standardizes a
long-format assay table, constructs the response, records the reference
condition, and stores the technical design. Growth exponents can be estimated,
supplied, or fixed, with a dedicated set of control-well covariates if this
should differ from the downstream model design. Matched background reporters
can be calibrated by Huber regression, ordinary least squares, or direct
subtraction. Numeric design variables such as concentration index can be
retained as quantitative covariates, while plate, batch, and replicate labels
can be handled as factors.

`fit_destress()` fits the model-based workflow and stores response metadata,
growth-exponent estimates, background-calibration estimates, model settings,
reporter-perturbation effects, p-values, and adjusted p-values. Results are
exported with `results()`, inspected with `model_parameters()`, and converted
into directional hit calls with `call_hits()`. We use the model-based workflow
as the default path, while median-polish and legacy empty-vector-control
presets reproduce earlier project analyses and enable comparison with the
model-based estimand.

The software flow mirrors the statistical construction in the paper. First, a
long-format screen is mapped to an assay object with explicit columns for the
reporter signal, the growth signal, the promoter, the compound, the reference
condition, and technical covariates. Second, the response scale is constructed
from the reporter and growth summaries, optionally using an estimated
promoter-specific growth exponent and an empty-vector or other background
reporter. Third, the model-based analysis estimates reporter-perturbation effects,
applies the selected uncertainty model, adjusts p-values within the chosen
family, and returns directional calls. Finally, the same result table is used
for visualization, comparison with legacy analyses, and manuscript-scale
exports.

For a generic arrayed reporter screen without a matched background reporter,
the complete model-based workflow can be written as:

```{r}
#| eval: false
library(DStressR)

assay <- prepare_assay(
  screen_table,
  promoter = "promoter",
  compound = "compound",
  control = "DMSO",
  lux = "lux_auc",
  growth = "od_fixed_time",
  growth_exponent = "estimate",
  batch = "plate",
  replicate = "replicate"
)

fit <- fit_destress(
  assay,
  preset = "model",
  technical = c("plate", "replicate"),
  empirical_bayes = TRUE,
  adjustment = "by_promoter"
)

pair_results <- results(fit)
hits <- call_hits(pair_results, fdr = 0.05, effect = "specific_effect")
```

When a matched empty-vector or background reporter is available, it enters
during response construction rather than as a separate legacy analysis:

```{r}
#| eval: false
assay_evc <- prepare_assay(
  screen_table,
  promoter = "promoter",
  compound = "compound",
  control = "DMSO",
  lux = "lux_auc",
  growth = "od_fixed_time",
  growth_exponent = "estimate",
  batch = "plate",
  replicate = "replicate",
  background_promoter = "EVC",
  background_method = "huber",
  background_by = c("compound", "plate", "replicate")
)

fit_evc <- fit_destress(
  assay_evc,
  preset = "model",
  technical = c("plate", "replicate"),
  empirical_bayes = TRUE,
  adjustment = "by_promoter"
)
```

The fitted object retains the model settings and intermediate quantities used
in the statistical analysis:

```{r}
#| eval: false
model_parameters(fit_evc)
head(results(fit_evc))

plot_volcano(
  results(fit_evc),
  effect = "specific_effect",
  padj = "specific_padj"
)

plot_response_heatmap(
  results(fit_evc),
  value = "specific_effect"
)
```

Optional model extensions use the same assay object and change only the
modeling layer. For example, a low-rank background adjustment or a full
promoter-by-compound interaction model can be requested explicitly:

```{r}
#| eval: false
fit_low_rank <- fit_destress(
  assay_evc,
  preset = "model",
  technical = c("plate", "replicate"),
  empirical_bayes = TRUE,
  background_rank = 1
)

fit_interaction <- fit_destress(
  assay_evc,
  preset = "model",
  technical = c("plate", "replicate"),
  empirical_bayes = TRUE,
  interaction = TRUE
)
```

For CRAN readiness, raw-data preparation and manuscript-scale analyses are kept
outside the installed package. The package ships compact, documented public
data derived from the published *E. coli* promoter-compound screen
[@Binsfeld2025PLoSBiol], together with vignettes and tests that exercise the
exported workflow. Full application scripts remain in the source repository so
that the manuscript analyses can be rerun without increasing the installed
package footprint.

\clearpage

### Supplementary Note B: Legacy Estimator Definitions {.unnumbered}

The package also retains two project-level estimators for reproducibility of
earlier analyses: a median-polish estimator and a legacy empty-vector-control
estimator. Both start from pre-normalized reporter responses, construct
replicate-level z-test p-values from DMSO or other reference wells, aggregate
replicate evidence conservatively at the promoter-compound level, and adjust
p-values within promoter. These estimators are useful for reproducing earlier
screen-specific workflows, but they are not the default statistical target of
the present paper.

### B.1 Median-Polish Workflow {.unnumbered}

The median-polish estimator follows the project-level analysis described
in @Alarcon2025Thesis. It starts from a pre-normalized response $u_{hk}$, where
$h$ denotes a promoter-library-plate-replicate group and $k$ denotes a compound
or control well. If $\mathcal d_h$ is the set of DMSO wells in group $h$, the
DMSO-centered response is

\begin{equation}
\label{eq:median-polish-dmso-centering}
m_{hk}
  =
  u_{hk}
  -
  \frac{1}{|\mathcal{d}_h|}
  \sum_{k' \in \mathcal{d}_h} u_{hk'} .
\end{equation}

Median polish decomposes the group-by-compound matrix as

\begin{equation}
\label{eq:median-polish-decomposition}
m_{hk}
  =
  \eta^{\mathrm{mp}}
  +
  \rho_h^{\mathrm{mp}}
  +
  \kappa_k^{\mathrm{mp}}
  +
  r_{hk}^{\mathrm{mp}},
\end{equation}

where $r_{hk}^{\mathrm{mp}}$ is the residual used for testing. Within each
group, the DMSO residuals define the Gaussian null used for the z test,
with $\bar r_{h\mathcal{d}}^{\mathrm{mp}}$ and
$s_{h\mathcal{d}}^{\mathrm{mp}}$ denoting the mean and standard deviation of
$r_{hk}^{\mathrm{mp}}$ over $k\in\mathcal d_h$:

\begin{equation}
\label{eq:median-polish-null}
\begin{aligned}
T_{hk}^{\mathrm{mp}}
  &=
  \frac{r_{hk}^{\mathrm{mp}} - \bar r_{h\mathcal{d}}^{\mathrm{mp}}}
       {s_{h\mathcal{d}}^{\mathrm{mp}}},\\
\pi_{hk}
  &=
  2\,\Pr\{Z \ge |T_{hk}^{\mathrm{mp}}|\},
  \qquad Z\sim\mathcal N(0,1).
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}

Mapping each group $h$ back to promoter $a$ and replicate context $t$ gives
replicate-level p-values $\pi_{ajt}$. For each promoter-compound pair, DStressR
keeps the conservative aggregate

\begin{equation}
\label{eq:median-polish-pvalue-aggregation}
\pi_{aj}^{\mathrm{pair}}
  =
  \max_t \pi_{ajt},
\end{equation}

followed by Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment within promoter. The normality of
the DMSO-centered null values can be assessed with the Lilliefors test
[@Lilliefors1967].

In the R package, the workflow can be called either directly or through the
legacy preset:

```{r}
#| eval: false
# Direct legacy estimator
mp_fit <- fit_median_polish(
  screen_table,
  response = "response",
  promoter = "promoter",
  compound = "compound",
  control = c("DMSO1", "DMSO2"),
  replicate = "replicate"
)

# Equivalent preset interface
mp_fit <- fit_destress(
  screen_table,
  preset = "median_polish",
  response = "response",
  promoter = "promoter",
  compound = "compound",
  control = c("DMSO1", "DMSO2"),
  replicate = "replicate"
)
```

### B.2 Empty-Vector-Control Workflow {.unnumbered}

The legacy empty-vector-control estimator follows @Alarcon2025Thesis and the
StressRegNet empty-vector-control application of @Amstalden2026StressRegNet.
It starts from a pre-normalized, median-centered reporter response $u_{ajt}$,
where $t$ indexes replicate observations, and uses a reporter strain without
promoter insert, denoted $e$, to estimate compound-specific reporter
background. For compound $j$, let $\mathcal r_e(j)$ denote the retained
empty-vector replicate observations. The empty-vector baseline is

\begin{equation}
\label{eq:empty-vector-baseline}
\bar u_{ej}
  =
  \frac{1}{|\mathcal r_e(j)|}
  \sum_{t \in \mathcal r_e(j)} u_{ejt}.
\end{equation}

Each reporter observation is transformed to an empty-vector fold change,

\begin{equation}
\label{eq:empty-vector-fold-change}
q_{ajt}
  =
  u_{ajt} - \bar u_{ej}.
\end{equation}

DMSO values within promoter-replicate strata define the null. Here
$\bar q_{a0t}$ and $s_{a0t}$ denote the mean and standard deviation of the
empty-vector-adjusted DMSO values for promoter $a$ and replicate stratum $t$:

\begin{equation}
\label{eq:empty-vector-null}
\begin{aligned}
T_{ajt}^{\mathrm{evc}}
  &=
  \frac{q_{ajt} - \bar q_{a0t}}
       {s_{a0t}},\\
\pi_{ajt}
  &=
  2\,\Pr\{Z \ge |T_{ajt}^{\mathrm{evc}}|\},
  \qquad Z\sim\mathcal N(0,1).
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}

As in the median-polish estimator, DStressR keeps the largest replicate-level
p-value for each promoter-compound pair and applies within-promoter
Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment. The DMSO empty-vector-adjusted values within
each promoter-replicate stratum can again be assessed with the Lilliefors test
[@Lilliefors1967].

In the R package, the workflow can again be called directly or through the
legacy preset:

```{r}
#| eval: false
# Direct legacy estimator
evc_fit <- fit_empty_vector_control(
  screen_table,
  response = "response",
  promoter = "promoter",
  compound = "compound",
  empty_vector = "EVC",
  control = c("DMSO1", "DMSO2"),
  replicate = "replicate"
)

# Equivalent preset interface
evc_fit <- fit_destress(
  screen_table,
  preset = "evc",
  response = "response",
  promoter = "promoter",
  compound = "compound",
  empty_vector = "EVC",
  control = c("DMSO1", "DMSO2"),
  replicate = "replicate"
)
```

\clearpage

### Supplementary Note C: Empirical-Bayes Variance Moderation {.unnumbered}

This supplementary note gives the moment calculation used for the prior degrees of
freedom in the moderated test. The model is the scaled inverse-$\chi^2$
empirical-Bayes variance model underlying moderated $t$ tests in `limma`
[@Smyth2004limmaEB; @Ritchie2015limma]. Let $v_\omega$ denote the raw
model-based variance for tested contrast $\omega$, and let $\nu$ denote the
residual degrees of freedom used for the ordinary $t$ statistic. DStressR uses

\begin{equation}
\label{eq:appendix-eb-sampling-model}
v_\omega \mid \sigma_\omega^2
  \sim
  \sigma_\omega^2 \frac{\chi^2_\nu}{\nu},
\qquad
\sigma_\omega^2
  \sim
  s_0^2 \frac{\nu_0}{\chi^2_{\nu_0}}.
\end{equation}

Equivalently, the marginal variance estimate follows

\begin{equation}
\label{eq:appendix-eb-f-model}
v_\omega
  \sim
  s_0^2 F_{\nu,\nu_0}.
\end{equation}

On the logarithmic scale, the first two moments are

\begin{equation}
\label{eq:appendix-eb-log-mean}
\mathbb E\{\log v_\omega\}
  =
  \log s_0^2
  +
  \psi(\nu/2)-\log(\nu/2)
  -
  \psi(\nu_0/2)+\log(\nu_0/2),
\end{equation}

and

\begin{equation}
\label{eq:appendix-eb-log-variance}
\operatorname{Var}\{\log v_\omega\}
  =
  \psi_1(\nu/2)+\psi_1(\nu_0/2),
\end{equation}

where $\psi$ is the digamma function and $\psi_1$ is the trigamma function.
Writing $\widehat{\operatorname{Var}}\{\log v_\omega\}$ for the empirical
variance of finite positive log-variance estimates, the prior degrees of
freedom are estimated by

\begin{equation}
\label{eq:appendix-eb-prior-df}
\widehat{\nu}_0
  =
  2\,
  \psi_1^{-1}
  \left[
    \widehat{\operatorname{Var}}\{\log v_\omega\}
    -
    \psi_1(\nu/2)
  \right],
\end{equation}

with a large prior-degree cap when the empirical excess variance is
non-positive. Given $\widehat{\nu}_0$, the prior variance is estimated as

\begin{equation}
\label{eq:appendix-eb-prior-variance}
\log \widehat{s}_0^2
  =
  \overline{\log v_\omega}
  -
  \psi(\nu/2)+\log(\nu/2)
  +
  \psi(\widehat{\nu}_0/2)-\log(\widehat{\nu}_0/2).
\end{equation}

The moderated variance and moderated statistic are then

\begin{equation}
\label{eq:appendix-eb-moderated-statistic}
\widetilde v_\omega
  =
  \frac{\nu v_\omega+\widehat{\nu}_0\widehat{s}_0^2}
       {\nu+\widehat{\nu}_0},
\qquad
\widetilde t_\omega
  =
  \frac{\widehat{\Delta}_\omega}{\sqrt{\widetilde v_\omega}},
\end{equation}

and the moderated p-value is evaluated against a
$t_{\nu+\widehat{\nu}_0}$ reference distribution.

### Supplementary Note E: E. coli DStressR Analysis with the Full Interaction Model {.unnumbered}

```{r}

interaction_dims <- rbind(
  read.delim(file.path(interaction_dir, "interaction_without_ev_model_matrix.tsv")),
  read.delim(file.path(interaction_dir, "interaction_with_ev_model_matrix.tsv"))
)
interaction_dims$response_modeling <- ifelse(
  grepl("_with_ev$", interaction_dims$analysis),
  "with EVC",
  "without EVC"
)
interaction_dims$inference <- ifelse(
  interaction_dims$model == "interaction",
  "interaction",
  "additive"
)
interaction_dims <- interaction_dims[, c(
  "response_modeling", "inference", "n_observations",
  "n_coefficients", "residual_df", "sigma"
)]
interaction_dims$sigma <- signif(interaction_dims$sigma, digits = 3)
names(interaction_dims) <- c(
  "Response modeling", "Inference", "N", "Coefficients", "Residual df", "Sigma"
)
if (knitr::is_latex_output()) {
  cat("\\begin{table}[H]\n")
  cat("\\caption{Design-matrix dimensions for the additive and full interaction models fitted to the WT \\textit{E. coli} screen.}\n")
  cat("\\centering\\begingroup\\small\\setlength{\\tabcolsep}{4pt}\n")
}
cat(knitr::kable(
  interaction_dims,
  format = if (knitr::is_latex_output()) "latex" else "pipe",
  booktabs = knitr::is_latex_output()
), sep = "\n")
if (knitr::is_latex_output()) {
  cat("\n\\endgroup\\end{table}\n")
}
```

The WT *E. coli* screen was small enough to fit the optional full
promoter-by-compound interaction model described in Section 2.4.
This is a downstream testing model for the already constructed DStressR
response; it is not an additional response-modeling step. The tested grid
contains 7 non-empty-vector promoters and 94 non-water compounds, yielding 658
tested promoter-compound pairs. Water is the reference condition. With
treatment coding, $a_i$ denotes the tested promoter for observation $i$, $j_i$
denotes one of the 95 condition levels including Water, $\lambda_{a_i}\in
\mathbb{R}^{6}$ is the promoter indicator vector, $\kappa_{j_i}\in
\mathbb{R}^{94}$ is the non-water condition indicator vector, and
$x_i\in\mathbb{R}^{2}$ contains the technical covariates replicate and dose
level. Let
$\widehat y_i$ denote the final response after growth-response modeling and,
for the EVC workflow, EVC calibration. The concrete full interaction model
fitted in this supplementary note is

\begin{equation}
\label{eq:appendix-ecoli-interaction-model-concrete}
\widehat y_i =
\beta_0
+ \lambda_{a_i}^{\top}\beta
+ \kappa_{j_i}^{\top}\theta
+ x_i^{\top}\zeta
+ (\lambda_{a_i}\otimes \kappa_{j_i})^{\top}\phi
+ \varepsilon_i,
\qquad
\varepsilon_i \sim \mathcal N(0,\sigma^2),
\end{equation}

where $\beta\in\mathbb{R}^{6}$, $\theta\in\mathbb{R}^{94}$,
$\zeta\in\mathbb{R}^{2}$, and $\phi\in\mathbb{R}^{564}$ contains the optional
promoter-by-compound interaction coefficients. Thus, the fitted interaction
model has

\begin{equation}
\label{eq:appendix-ecoli-interaction-coefficients}
1 + 6 + 94 + 2 + (6 \times 94) = 667
\end{equation}

coefficients. The corresponding additive model omits $\phi$ and therefore has
103 coefficients. The uncalibrated interaction run uses $M=5148$ observations.
The empty-vector-calibrated interaction run uses $M=5127$ observations after
response-level calibration and removal of the empty-vector reporter from the
tested promoter set. Both runs use moderated $t$ tests, within-promoter
Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment, and FDR 0.05 for hit calling.

![Joint hit-set intersections for the Binsfeld reference rule, the two primary DStressR analyses, and the two DStressR analyses with the full interaction model. The Venn-style panel shows the five compared hit sets, with numbers placed directly on the corresponding non-empty intersections. The central overlap contains 28 pairs called by all five analyses.](../../analysis/outputs/ecoli_interaction_model/interaction_joint_venn_plot.png){#fig-appendix-ecoli-interaction-hit-overlap width="100%" fig-align="center"}

![Comparison between the primary additive DStressR analyses and the optional full interaction models. Points show promoter-compound pairs from the WT *E. coli* screen; the dashed diagonal marks equality of effect estimates.](../../analysis/outputs/ecoli_interaction_model/interaction_effect_comparison.png){#fig-appendix-ecoli-interaction-effect-comparison width="80%" fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-ecoli-interaction-key-pairs
#| tbl-cap: "Selected promoter-compound pairs comparing primary additive analyses with full interaction-model analyses. Hit-set codes: Ref, Binsfeld reference; NoE, DStressR without EVC; EVC, DStressR with EVC; IntN, full interaction model without EVC; IntE, full interaction model with EVC."

key_pairs <- read.delim(
  file.path(interaction_dir, "interaction_key_pair_comparison.tsv"),
  check.names = FALSE
)

  "promoter", "compound", "binsfeld_hit", "modeled_hit",
  "evc_huber_hit", "interaction_without_ev_hit", "interaction_with_ev_hit",
  "modeled_effect", "evc_huber_effect",
  "interaction_without_ev_effect", "interaction_with_ev_effect",

  "interaction_with_ev_padj_by_promoter"
)]

  hits <- c(
    if (isTRUE(ref)) "Ref",
    if (isTRUE(no_evc)) "NoE",
    if (isTRUE(evc)) "EVC",
    if (isTRUE(int_no_evc)) "IntN",
    if (isTRUE(int_evc)) "IntE"
  )
  if (length(hits) == 0) "--" else paste(hits, collapse = ",")
}
key_pairs$hit_sets <- mapply(
  hit_code,
  key_pairs$binsfeld_hit,
  key_pairs$modeled_hit,
  key_pairs$evc_huber_hit,
  key_pairs$interaction_without_ev_hit,
  key_pairs$interaction_with_ev_hit,
  USE.NAMES = FALSE

  "modeled_effect", "evc_huber_effect",
  "interaction_without_ev_effect", "interaction_with_ev_effect",
  "modeled_padj_by_promoter", "evc_huber_padj_by_promoter",
  "interaction_without_ev_padj_by_promoter",
  "interaction_with_ev_padj_by_promoter"
)]
names(key_pairs) <- c(
  "Prom.", "Cmpd.", "Hits",
  "NoE eff.", "EVC eff.", "IntN eff.", "IntE eff.",
  "NoE q", "EVC q", "IntN q", "IntE q"
)
numeric_columns <- vapply(key_pairs, is.numeric, logical(1))
key_pairs[numeric_columns] <- lapply(key_pairs[numeric_columns], signif, digits = 3)
if (knitr::is_latex_output()) {
  cat("\\begingroup\\tiny\\setlength{\\tabcolsep}{1.2pt}\\resizebox{\\linewidth}{!}{%\n")
}
cat(knitr::kable(
  key_pairs,
  format = if (knitr::is_latex_output()) "latex" else "pipe",
  booktabs = knitr::is_latex_output()
), sep = "\n")
if (knitr::is_latex_output()) {
  cat("\n}\\endgroup\n")
}
```
